text: follow-on: loops 15 and 16 are marked corpus-validated although they pass on E100642 alone, which is the exact test the node uses to leave loops 1-6 and 8-11 source-only. CORPUS_VALIDATED_FROM = 12 (test line 50) and CORPUS_VALIDATED_FROM = 12 in the retarget script split the 26 loops at a loop number rather than by the fit evidence. The loop-reference RCA the node cites (docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-loop-reference-rca.html) records the pass sets the split contradicts: on E100579 'loops 12, 13, 14 and 18-27 pass while loops 1-6, 8-11, 15, 16 and 17 fail', and on E100595 'only loops 17-26 pass, while 1-6, 8-11, 12-16 and 27 fail'. So loop 15 and loop 16 pass on E100642 alone -- one shot, the same one-shot basis the node calls 'not fixed' for loops 1-6 and 17/comp: loops 15 and 16 are corpus-validated (a proven sign) while loops 1-6 and 8-11 with identical one-shot evidence are source-only. The code comment 'Loops 12-27 track on every shot the fits cover' is false for 15 and 16. Reproduced from the cited fragment's own pass counts; the map carries state corpus-validated on magFlxLp15 and magFlxLp16 (live map, target_index 40 and 41).

follow-on: _differential_flux_loop_targets fails open. It returns frozenset() whenever the store is not where it looked -- catalog has no maps, catalog.maps[0].name is not the magnetics store directory, or store.is_file() is false -- and the caller then passes differential_targets=frozenset() to _absolute_flux_loop_rules, which keeps every proven rule. On the retargeted JT-60SA map loops 7 and 12-27 are corpus-validated, so an empty differential set admits all 17 as absolute flux loops, exactly the state the node exists to prevent (the cohort would read 17 channels instead of loop 7 alone). The store-name inference is the fragile part: the path is built from catalog.maps[0].name (line ~845), so a catalogue whose first map is not magnetics, or an entry-order change, silently redirects the read to a non-existent file and disables the guard rather than raising. A machine that genuinely declares no description store may reasonably yield no differential targets, but a declared store whose expected file is absent is a defect that should raise, not resolve to the permissive set.

follow-on: the run's positive-gate evidence is unsound as recorded. manifest.md asserts status complete and tests 'tests/data/test_jt60sa_signal_maps.py: 30 passed', but the only gate log it cites, /tmp/jtmm-gate.log, has a header reading 'revision: 5809ee027bd0ec8cc6cd4f5333da5ad6d328cf1a' -- the parent of the reviewed head 11ee0362, so it is not a head-revision arm -- and the log is truncated mid-run: it ends at '................................F...........' after a failing test with no summary line and no EXIT sentinel. The run's own final stream message reads 'The gate has one failure -- waiting for its summary to identify it before concluding', and exit.json records ended_during 'working', so the process ended before that gate finished. The manifest carries no baseline_suite and no after_suite, so the run supplies no completed positive arm at any revision. The claim is nevertheless independently reproducible -- I re-ran the gate at head 11ee0362 (1 failed, 87 passed, EXIT=1, the failure being the pre-existing unit-audit one) -- but the run's own record cannot support its 'complete' status or its passing count as cited. The negative control log is likewise labelled 'revision: 5809ee02 (+ exclusion removed)', a working-tree mutation at the parent revision rather than a head-revision control.

justifications.durability: A real, tested gain: the selection now excludes differential targets so a well-proven differential rule can no longer enter the absolute-flux response, the resolver reads the entry assignment from the description store so the store order is never assumed, and the retarget is a kept, re-runnable script. Points off for the fail-open path in _differential_flux_loop_targets -- a mis-located or absent store silently empties the differential set and re-admits all 17 proven loops -- and for the corpus-validated over-claim at loops 15, 16.
justifications.evidence: The head arm reproduces and the negative control is the strong form: I re-ran the gate at 11ee0362 (1 failed, 87 passed, EXIT=1) and reproduced the guard's firing at head (removing the exclusion line fails test_absolute_loop_selector_drops_a_proven_differential_entry and test_signal_map_reader_drops_a_proven_differential_loop, 2 failed EXIT=1), and verified both map digests on disk. The run's own record is unsound: no completed positive log at the head revision, a truncated parent-revision gate log with a failure, and a negative-control label at the parent revision. added_failure_count 0 is robust because the sole head failure is a base failure.
justifications.fit: Keeps the module's idiom: the docstring on _absolute_flux_loop_rules is rewritten to the new rule, the new resolver carries a full docstring, the selector's ValueError message is updated, and the test file uses the module's existing helpers. Points off for the code comment asserting loops 12-27 'track on every shot the fits cover', which the cited RCA's pass sets contradict for 15 and 16, and for the three-place duplication of the int32 fill sentinel.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The retarget lands and the selector does what the dispatch asked: every loop rule but the reference resolves to its type-6 pair entry with channel_factor -1, the resolver reads the pair assignment from the store rather than assuming order, and the cohort is narrowed to reference loop 7. Points off because loops 15 and 16 are stamped corpus-validated on a one-shot basis the node itself calls insufficient for loops 1-6/8-11 (finding 1), which is a physics-relevant over-claim about which loops carry a proven sign.
justifications.reuse: Good: the resolver reuses load_packaged_machine_map and description_store_root_path rather than a second catalogue reader, and the tests reuse _signal_rule/_stub_signal_maps rather than new fixtures. Points off for duplicating the -2147483647 fill constant in three places (cocos_convention._NO_DIFFERENTIAL_INDEX, the retarget script's _NO_INDEX, and a bare literal in the signal-maps test) and for inferring the store filename from catalog.maps[0].name rather than the magnetics entry the reader actually needs.
justifications.scope_discipline: Writes stayed within the declared paths; the two shared bundle map files were written as the coordinator's widening directed, and the map edit was scripted, never hand-edited (retarget_differential_loop_rules.py rewrites all 26 rules and prints both digests). No plan, index or sprint mutation, no stray files, worktree clean at head. One mark off only for the unversioned map edit, which is the design for this bundle (maps moved out of git) but means the landed change is attested only by digest.
